newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Two Moroccan sites seen as world heritage.
newsitem.headline: Two Moroccan sites seen as world heritage.

text.p: Two Moroccan sites, the Roman town of Volubilis and the northern mediaeval city of Tetuan, may be classed as part of the world's heritage by the United Nations, the official news agency MAP said.
Volubilis dates back to the fourth century BC, an official at the Culture Ministry said on Wednesday.

"The two sites have been recommended for registration on the list of world patrimony, whose session was held in Paris on June 23-28 at UNESCO headquarters," MAP quoted a culture ministry statement as saying.

Essaouira Medina, another site which can be traced back to the 18th century, was under examination and could be added to existing sites on the UNESCO list which includes medinas of Fez, Meknes and Marrakesh in central and southern Morocco.
